Blocks.Section: Generate a Token Manually Using the Developer Portal
SectionPath: Generate a Token Manually Using the Developer Portal
Blocks.Text: The LinkedIn Developer Portal has a token generator for manually creating tokens. Visit the LinkedIn Developer Portal Token Generator or follow the steps outlined in Developer Portal Tools.

Blocks.Section: Step 1: Get Client ID and Client Secret
SectionPath: Step 1: Get Client ID and Client Secret
Blocks.Text:
Getting started? Create a new application on the Developer Portal.
Existing application? Go to My apps to modify your app settings.

Blocks.Section: Step 1: Get Client ID and Client Secret
SectionPath: Step 1: Get Client ID and Client Secret
Blocks.Text: Each application is assigned a unique Client ID (Consumer key/API key) and Client Secret. Please make a note of these values as they will be integrated into your application config files. Your Client Secret protects your application's security so be sure to keep it secure!

Blocks.Section: Step 1: Get Client ID and Client Secret
SectionPath: Step 1: Get Client ID and Client Secret
Blocks.Text: Warning

Blocks.Section: Step 1: Get Client ID and Client Secret
SectionPath: Step 1: Get Client ID and Client Secret
Blocks.Text: Do not share your Client Secret value with anyone, and do not pass it in the URL when making API calls, or URI query-string parameters, or post in support forums, chat, etc.
To generate an access token, issue a HTTP POST against accessToken with a Content-Type header of x-www-form-urlencoded and the following parameters in the request body:
https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken

Rows.Text: The value of this field should always be client_credentials
The Client ID value generated when you registered your application
The Client Secret value generated when you registered your application

Blocks.Text: View the Best Practices for Secure Applications page for more security info.
A successful access token request returns a JSON object containing the following fields:

access_token — The access token for the application. This token must be kept secure.
expires_in — Seconds until token expiration.

The access token has a 30-minute lifespan and must be used immediately. You may request a new token once your current token expires.
Once you've received an access token, you can make API requests by including an Authorization header with your token in the HTTP call to LinkedIn's API.

GET https://api.linkedin.com/rest/simpleJobPostings

Connection: Keep-Alive
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Linkedin-Version: 202603
If you make an API call using an invalid token, you'll receive a 401 Unauthorized response from the server. In this case, the token may need to be regenerated because it expired or was revoked.
These are not the only reasons for an invalid token. Make sure your applications are coded to properly handle a 401 error.
